$comment: Human-readable text for walk-hallway 0.1.0 on hallway-open 0.1.0 (specs #30). Text only; README.md stays normative.

mission.title: Walk the hallway
mission.description: The robot starts at the hallway entrance and is commanded to walk straight ahead at 0.5 m/s. It must reach the exit, 5.5 m along the route, within 27 s, staying upright, never touching either wall, and staying within its lateral limit of the centreline.

success_criteria.text: Reaches the exit, 5.5 m along the route, within 27 s, crossing it inside the exit segment.
Stays upright: the base never drops below the fall height.
Stays within its lateral limit of the hallway centreline.

mission.grading: One run is one or more identical trials at the exact nominal pose. The default is 1. A grading policy turns trial outcomes into the run grade. A test-system ERROR is reported and excluded, and is never counted as a robot fail. A failed trial is not retried.
mission.time_limit_explained: 27 s is twice the time the route takes at the commanded speed, plus 5 s (2 × 5.5 m ÷ 0.5 m/s + 5 s).

world.title: Open hallway
world.description: A straight, empty hallway 1.50 m wide between the walls and 6.00 m long, with 2.50 m-high walls. Nothing else is in it: the test is whether the robot can hold a straight line.

lateral_limit.text: How far the robot's centre may drift from the centreline before its side would reach a wall: half the clear width minus half the robot's width.
lateral_limit.sentence: {robot} may drift up to {value} m either side of the centreline: half the {clear_width} m hallway, minus half its {robot_width} m width.

exit_segment.text: The exit counts only when the robot's base crosses it between the walls, within half the clear width of the centreline.

fall_height.text: The lowest base height that still counts as upright, declared by the selected configuration.

fits_width.text: Checked before any trial: the robot fits when its width plus the wall clearance on each side (0.05 m for a humanoid, 0.10 m for a quadruped) is at most the clear width. A robot that does not fit is UNSUPPORTED, not run.
